documents.title: Burning and cloudy urine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, since Saturday it burns when I cath and the urine is cloudy and smells off. No fever, back feels fine. This is what my infections usually feel like. Can I come in tomorrow?

documents.title: Re: Burning and cloudy urine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Colleen, yes — 9:40 tomorrow. Please bring a sample from a fresh catheter in a sterile cup (we'll leave a kit at the front if you need one, but a clean container from home is fine). If you get a fever, chills or back pain tonight, call the on-call line.

documents.title: Acute Visit — UTI symptoms
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 44F with neurogenic bladder on CIC, chronic Proteus colonization. 2 days of burning with catheterization, cloudy foul urine. No fever or chills, no flank pain, no increase in spasms. Says this is her typical infection.
O: afebrile, vitals reviewed and normal. Abdomen soft, mild suprapubic tenderness, no CVA tenderness.
UA in office: cloudy, pH 7.5, LE 2+, nitrite +, WBC 40/hpf, RBC 3/hpf. Culture sent.
A/P: symptomatic lower UTI, likely her usual Proteus. TMP-SMX contraindicated (SJS) and Proteus is intrinsically resistant to nitrofurantoin, so cephalexin 500 mg BID x 7 days. Will adjust to culture. Fluids, continue CIC schedule. Call for fever or flank pain.

documents.title: Urine culture result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Culture back: Proteus mirabilis >100K, sensitive to cephalexin. Called pt — already feeling better, burning nearly gone, no fever. Finish all 7 days. PCP aware, no change.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis, compared with 2023 and 2021. Scattered fibroglandular densities. No suspicious findings.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Screening mammogram negative. Next one in a year.

documents.title: Oxybutynin refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic refill request oxybutynin 5 mg TID #270. Last visit 09/2023, physical due Sept. Approved by PCP x 90 days + 1 refill.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
44F, yearly visit.

Since last year: one Proteus UTI in February, treated with cephalexin, resolved. Otherwise well. Cathing q4-6h. Bowel program fine. Work steady.
Meds: oxybutynin 5 TID, methenamine 1 g BID, docusate 100 BID. Allergies: TMP-SMX (SJS), latex.

Exam: BP and vitals at goal. Well appearing. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign, no CVA tenderness. Breast exam normal. Sacrum/heels intact. LE neuro at baseline.
PHQ-9 1.

A/P:
- Neurogenic bladder / recurrent UTI / chronic Proteus: stable, urology in Nov.
- HM: flu and updated COVID given. CMP, CBC, lipids. Mammogram current (3/2024). Colon screening when she turns 45 in December — will send FIT after that. Pap due 2026.
RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All normal again — kidney function, blood counts, liver and cholesterol. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Urology follow-up letter
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group. Visit 11/19/2024.

Annual review for neurogenic bladder after T12 cord injury. Managing well with clean intermittent catheterization. Noted one cystitis episode in February treated in your office with cephalexin; culture Proteus mirabilis as expected. No febrile infections.

Allergies: TMP-SMX (SJS), latex.
Current medications: oxybutynin 5 mg TID, methenamine hippurate 1 g BID, docusate sodium 100 mg BID.

Exam: unremarkable abdomen, no flank tenderness.

Plan: continue current program. See again in 12 months.

Urology

documents.title: Colon screening
documents.author: patient
documents.body: You mentioned the colon test after I turned 45. Can I do the at-home kit? A colonoscopy prep sounds rough with my bowel routine.

documents.title: Re: Colon screening
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, FIT is a good choice for you. Ordered — the lab will mail the kit. It's one sample, no diet changes. If it's ever positive we'd talk about colonoscopy then.

documents.title: FIT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative. Portal note sent; repeat yearly.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis, compared with prior studies. Scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No mass, suspicious calcifications or distortion.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Negative mammogram. Annual.

documents.title: Cancellation
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to cancel tomorrow's check-in — work deadline. Nothing urgent, feels fine. Will keep the September physical instead.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional emergency department. Date of visit 06/17/2025. Received by fax.

CC: R flank pain, burning x2 days.
HPI: 45 y/o F, neurogenic bladder from T12 SCI on intermittent cath. Two days of right-sided flank pain, steady, moving down into the groin. Burning with urination, constant urge, getting only small volumes of cloudy urine. No fever. No nausea or vomiting.
PMH: neurogenic bladder, recurrent UTIs, chronic Proteus bacteriuria. PSH: appendectomy.
Home meds: oxybutynin, methenamine, docusate.
Allergies: TMP-SMX (SJS), LATEX.
SH: former smoker, no EtOH. FH: mother with kidney stones.

Exam: uncomfortable, shifting in bed. Afebrile. Right CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft, no peritoneal signs.
UA: pH 8.5, pyuria, crystals seen on microscopy. Gram stain of urine: no organisms.

MDM: presentation consistent with right renal colic in a patient with a family history of stones. No signs of infection on stain, afebrile. Pain controlled.
Dx: urolithiasis / right renal colic.
Disposition: home. Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, acetaminophen 1 g q6h prn. Strain urine. Follow up with urology and PCP this week. Return for fever, vomiting, uncontrolled pain.

documents.title: Went to the ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI I was in the ER last night with right side pain — they think a kidney stone. My mom has had these forever so I guess it was my turn. They gave me tamsulosin and said strain my urine. Pain is better this morning. Do you need to see me?

documents.title: Re: Went to the ER last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry you went through that. Their record just came in. Yes, let's see you next Tuesday and check kidney function. Keep the tamsulosin going and strain everything. Fever, vomiting or pain you can't control = back to the ED or call me directly. I'll let your urologist's office know too.

events.reason: follow-up after ED visit for kidney stone

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in ED 6/17 with right renal colic. ED record reviewed: afebrile, R CVA tenderness, UA pH 8.5 with pyuria and crystals, no organisms on stain. Discharged on tamsulosin and acetaminophen.

Today: pain much better, occasional ache. Nothing caught in the strainer yet. No fever, no vomiting. Urgency improving. Taking tamsulosin without dizziness.

Exam: afebrile, vitals fine. Mild R CVA tenderness, abdomen soft.

A/P: kidney stone, right, improving. Continue tamsulosin, keep straining and bring in anything she catches. BMP today. Urology office contacted, she has an appointment in late summer. Fluids. Same red flags.
Meds now: oxybutynin, methenamine, docusate, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily.

documents.title: Kidney function
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine is 0.9, same as your usual — the kidney is working fine. Keep straining and keep the urology appointment.

documents.title: Urology visit letter
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group. Visit 09/04/2025.

Seen after her June ED visit for right renal colic. Flank pain has settled; no stone recovered. Since June she has had persistent urgency with small-volume voids between catheterizations.

Allergies: TMP-SMX (SJS), latex.
Medications: oxybutynin 5 mg TID, methenamine hippurate 1 g BID, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, docusate 100 mg BID.

Plan: we placed an indwelling urethral catheter today (16 Fr silicone, latex-free) for bladder management, to be changed monthly by our nursing staff. Continue tamsulosin, oxybutynin and methenamine. Return in 3 months, sooner with fever.

Urology

documents.title: Catheter bag question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick question — urology put in a catheter last week. Is it okay to keep the leg bag on overnight or do I need the big night bag? They gave me both and I forgot what they said.

documents.title: Re: Catheter bag question
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Use the larger night drainage bag overnight and keep it below bladder level; switch back to the leg bag in the morning. Rinse bags per the supply instructions. Call urology's nurse line or us if the catheter stops draining.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
45F, annual.

Interval: ED in June for right renal colic, settled; no stone recovered. Urology switched her to an indwelling catheter on 9/4, changed monthly at their office. Says it's easier day to day, though she misses the independence of cathing. No fever.
Meds: oxybutynin 5 TID, methenamine 1 g BID, tamsulosin 0.4 daily, docusate 100 BID. Allergies: TMP-SMX (SJS), latex.

Exam: well. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no CVA tenderness today. Catheter draining clear yellow urine, meatus without irritation. Skin intact. Breast exam normal.
PHQ-9 2.

A/P:
- Neurogenic bladder, now indwelling catheter per urology. Reviewed catheter care and when to call (fever, flank pain, poor drainage).
- Kidney stone, right: asymptomatic. Urology following.
- Recurrent UTI/Proteus: no treatment of colonization.
- HM: flu and updated COVID today. CMP, CBC, lipids. FIT negative 1/2025, repeat in January. Mammogram 3/2025 normal. Pap/HPV due next year.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs normal, including kidney function, calcium and cholesterol. Have a good fall.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional emergency department, visit 10/19/2025. Received electronically.

CC: fever, R flank pain, burning.
HPI: 45F with neurogenic bladder (T12 SCI), recurrent UTIs and known Proteus colonization, with an indwelling urethral catheter for the past several weeks. Presents with fever, right flank pain and dysuria. Seen here in June for right renal colic.
Meds: oxybutynin, methenamine, tamsulosin, docusate. Allergies: TMP-SMX (SJS), latex.

Triage: T 38.6 C, HR 102, BP 124/76, RR 18, SpO2 98% RA.
Exam: ill-appearing but nontoxic. Right CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft. Catheter in place, cloudy urine in bag.
UA: alkaline (pH 8.5); microscopy with rectangular prism-shaped crystals. Urine culture sent from the new catheter.
KUB: radiopaque calculus over the right renal shadow.

Course: ceftriaxone 1 g IV. Catheter exchanged for a new latex-free catheter. Defervesced, tolerating PO.
Dx: catheter-associated UTI; right renal calculus.
Dispo: home on ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID x 7 days (TMP-SMX allergy). Urology follow-up for the stone. PCP within a week. Return for rigors, vomiting, worsening pain.

documents.title: Post-ED call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after ED visit Sunday. ED culture resulted this morning: Proteus mirabilis, sensitive to cipro. Pt on day 3 of ciprofloxacin, no fever since Sunday night, flank pain easing. Catheter draining well. Booked with PCP 10/28. Advised to call if fever returns.

events.reason: follow-up after ED visit for urinary infection

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED 10/19: fever, R flank pain, dysuria with indwelling catheter. Alkaline urine with prism-shaped crystals, KUB with a right renal calculus. Ceftriaxone in ED, catheter exchanged, home on cipro x7d. Culture Proteus mirabilis, cipro-sensitive.

Today: finishing cipro tomorrow. No fever for a week, flank pain gone. Catheter working.
Exam: afebrile, vitals normal. No CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft.

A/P: catheter-associated Proteus UTI, resolved clinically. Right renal calculus on KUB — the alkaline urine and crystals with Proteus raise the question of an infection-related stone; urology needs to see the film. Sent ED records to urology and asked for a sooner visit. Continue current meds.

documents.title: Urology follow-up letter
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group. Visit 12/09/2025.

Follow-up after the October ED visit for a febrile catheter-associated Proteus infection. Afebrile since. We reviewed the ED KUB, which shows a right renal calculus. Given her alkaline urine and Proteus history this is likely an infection stone and will need definitive treatment.

Allergies: TMP-SMX (SJS), latex.
Medications: oxybutynin 5 mg TID, methenamine hippurate 1 g BID, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, docusate 100 mg BID.

Plan: non-contrast CT abdomen and pelvis to define the stone burden before planning surgery; our office will schedule it. Indwelling catheter changes continue monthly. Return after CT.

Urology
